messages:
jamie: Customer seeing streaming cutout then 401 on reconnect. App: AcmeAnalytics. Need a minimal curl repro + debug bundle. x-request-id: rqd-ACM-7f1a. Help?
maria: Can you paste the exact x-request-id from the response and any trace id? Region/model?
jamie: Sure — x-request-id: rqd-ACM-7f1a; x-trace-id: trace-9f4b; region: us-west-2; model: gpt-open-3b-quant. Failure around 30–60s: stream stops, client reconnect gets 401.
ashok: Start by running a minimal streaming curl. Replace <TOKEN> and make sure the X-Request-ID header is set.
ashok: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: rqd-ACM-7f1a" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-open-3b-quant"
```
maria: When you run that, capture the -v output and also run with --raw or --no-buffer to preserve chunking. If they're behind a corporate proxy add --proxy.
ashok: If the reconnect returns 401, capture response headers: Date, x-auth-expiry, set-cookie, and any WWW-Authenticate. Also capture TLS info with curl -Iv.
jamie: Pasting a short excerpt from the customer logs (redacted):
jamie: ```
[2024-03-28T15:02:43Z] CONNECT -> 200 OK, streaming
[2024-03-28T15:03:25Z] stream chunk received, user payload
[2024-03-28T15:03:25Z] connection reset by peer
[2024-03-28T15:03:26Z] RECONNECT -> 401 Unauthorized, x-request-id: rqd-ACM-7f1a
set-cookie: auth=deleted; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
x-auth-expiry: 1700000000
```
support-bot: debug-bundle created for thread 1745559999: https://files.redwood.internal/debug/1745559999-acme-bundle.zip (redacted). Include both a successful run and a failing run.
elaine: Also ask customer to capture client-side pcap/tcpdump for the window around the disconnect (1m before/after). If using node SDK suggest NODE_DEBUG=request to surface socket timing.
maria: Before we hand this to infra, confirm the exact curl you used. I tried a reproduction in us-west-2 with the same model and token and saw a steady stream for 2m — so we may be hitting a proxy or auth-window issue on customer's side.
jamie: Uploaded bundle and curl outputs to ticket #3429. My local test with --no-buffer reproduced EOF at ~43s. Command I used:
jamie: ```
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: rqd-ACM-7f1a" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-open-3b-quant" > curl_run_1.log
```
ashok: Thanks — I'll run the bundle and try a proxy replay. Also include x-customer-billing: acme-999 in headers so we can correlate billing spikes and check for mid-window token rotation logic.
maria: One more server-side id would help: server log id for that window (if you have it). Also note UTC window for events so we can assemble traces.
jamie: Got server id: srv-7f1a. Window: 2024-03-28T15:02:30Z → 2024-03-28T15:04:00Z. I've asked customer to sign off on the pcap upload.
elaine: If we can't repro internally, we'll ask infra to run a sticky session test and a token-rotation test against the dedicated edge in us-west-2.
jamie: Thanks everyone — bundle link and curl logs are in ticket #3429. I'll post updates after the proxy replay. :thumbsup:
